self.dialectNote: Vietnamese uses a pronominal kinship system (xưng hô) where self-referent terms change depending on the addressee's age and status. tôi is neutral/formal; mình is friendly/informal; con (to elders); anh/chị (to peers or younger); em (to elders, as younger). Northern speakers use tao/mày with close friends. Southern speakers use tui casually.

xungHo.contextNote: Vietnamese uses a pronominal kinship system (xưng hô) where self-referent terms change depending on the addressee's age and status. There is no single word for 'I' — the term is always relational.

relationships.englishTerm: Father

xungHo.addressTerm: bố / cha / ba
xungHo.contextNote: Child calls themselves 'con' (I) and addresses father as 'bố/cha/ba'. The father calls himself 'bố/ba/cha' and addresses the child as 'con'.

relationships.toneNote: bố (Northern) has sắc tone — must not be confused with bò (huyền, ox), bổ (hỏi), bỗ (ngã), bộ (nặng). ba (Southern) uses ngang tone — distinct from bà (huyền, grandmother), bả (hỏi), bã (ngã), bá (sắc), bạ (nặng).
relationships.teknonymyPattern: bố [tên con cả] / cha [tên con cả]
relationships.dialectNote: Northern (Hà Nội): bố dominates everyday speech; cha is formal/literary. Southern (Sài Gòn/Mekong): ba is nearly universal colloquially. Central (Huế, Đà Nẵng): ba or cha. Hà Tĩnh/Nghệ An: bọ is distinctive. Mekong Delta: tía survives in older communities. Classical: cha or phụ (Hán-Việt). cha is the most formal and universally understood written form across all dialects.

relationships.dialectNote: Standard and Northern: mẹ is universal, both formal and colloquial. Southern: má dominates colloquially; mẹ is understood but less used daily. Central (Huế): mạ or mẹ. Hà Tĩnh/Nghệ An: mạ is common. Classical: mẫu thân (Hán-Việt). mẹ is the most universally understood.

metadata.kinshipSystem: Vietnamese Bifurcate-Collateral with Obligatory Relative-Age Distinction and Pronoun-Kinship Fusion (xưng hô system, Confucian thứ bậc hierarchy)
metadata.specialNote: Vietnamese kinship is unique for: (1) Pronoun-kinship fusion — xưng hô system means kinship terms ARE the first/second person pronouns; (2) Mandatory relative-age distinction for parent's siblings — bác vs chú/cô/cậu/dì — getting this wrong is a social error; (3) cháu is both grandchild and niece/nephew depending on speaker generation; (4) Three writing systems: Chữ Quốc ngữ, Chữ Nôm, Hán-Việt.
